The intra-modal stream, inspired by the hippocampus, employs a semantic memory module and a sparse activation network to reconstruct missing features within each modality. This stream leverages modality-specific information to fill in gaps caused by missing data, aiming to preserve the integrity of individual modality representations. The inter-modal stream, drawing inspiration from the thalamus, utilizes a confidence-perception module and a cross-modal completion module to integrate information across modalities. This stream dynamically weights the contribution of each modality based on its perceived confidence, suppressing redundant information and focusing on reliable cross-modal cues. The model's architecture is further enhanced by a hierarchical fusion module that combines the outputs of the two streams.
